## Natural history notes

A small jewel beetle characterized by a hard, narrow, bullet-shaped body, dark coloration with pale or yellowish spotting or banding, and a compact form typical of flower-visiting buprestids. In Florida, Acmaeodera tubulus is most likely encountered in warm dry or semi-open habitats such as scrub, sandhills, pine flatwoods, forest edges, and flowering patches where adults visit blossoms. Adults feed on pollen or nectar at flowers, while the larvae of related Acmaeodera species develop in dead or dying woody material, so this species is best treated cautiously as a wood-associated beetle that contributes to decomposition and serves as prey for birds, lizards, spiders, and predatory insects.
